coverageGaps.reason: ships 1,500+ deterministic rules and 100 LLM rules — unobservable via CLI (pending review). The claim asserts a SPLIT (deterministic vs LLM) and `truecourse rules list`'s promised output — `Rules for <repo>: N shown (E enabled, D disabled)` plus per-rule rows of key / status / [domain/severity] / language support / name — carries no deterministic-vs-LLM label. Asserting only the total (>1,600 rows) would be a green that does not prove its claim, exactly the defect class the fidelity judge exists to catch. Two ways out, both for the user to choose: label the kind in `rules list` output, or narrow the doc claim.

the per-file budget defaults to 30 seconds — unobservable via CLI (pending review). Nothing prints the effective budget, so the only proof is a wall-clock measurement: a file that must survive 29s and be skipped at 31s. That is a minutes-long, machine-speed dependent scenario — the flakiness it buys is worse than the coverage. The override claim (`TRUECOURSE_DET_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS`) IS carried, in `survive-a-file-that-exceeds-the-per-file-budget`.

C# is supported with the .NET 8 SDK — needs dotnet-sdk. A supplied dependency with no registered instance: the .NET 8 SDK plus the Roslyn host built from the TrueCourse source tree. Register one and this becomes a flow (seed a `.cs` file, assert a violation against it) — the scenario is blocked, not impossible.

C# semantic rules need the Roslyn host built once — needs dotnet-sdk, and the documented build command (`dotnet build -c Release tools/csharp-roslyn-host`) points INSIDE the TrueCourse source tree, which a user who installed from npm does not have. Blocked on both the supplied SDK and a doc/interface answer to "where does an installed user build the host from".

disabling a rule removes its detection and LLM cost — llm-cost plus an unassertable comparison. The falsifiable half is "the run's LLM call/token totals DROP after the rule is disabled", which needs two full LLM runs over the same project and a comparison BETWEEN their summaries; a scenario asserts per-step matchers, not deltas across steps, and the model's own output is not deterministic enough to assert the rule's absence directly.

.truecourseignore also narrows spec scan doc discovery — out of the authored interface set — the proof runs through `truecourse spec scan` and `.truecourse/specs/corpus.json`, and no `cli/spec` interface exists in reference/interfaces (the reference covers the code-analysis surface: analyze, add, list, rules, hooks, root). It also needs an LLM transport for a full scan. The claim belongs to a spec-scan area flow once that surface's interfaces are authored.

--llm runs the LLM rules for this run — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency: proving that an LLM rule RAN needs a live transport, which the reference corpus binds only where the flow is about the transport itself.

--llm pre-approves the cost estimate — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency: the cost estimate is only reachable on a run that would really call the model, and its absence must be observed on a terminal.

--llm-transport picks how the LLM is reached for this run — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency, and partly unrealizable: the doc's value set includes `agent`, which the post-Phase-0 target deletes (interface decision `phase-0-transport`), so one of the three documented values has no supported path to test.

--io sets the mailbox dir for the agent transport — unrealizable against the post-Phase-0 target: `--io` exists only to serve `--llm-transport agent`, which Phase 0 removes (interface decision `phase-0-transport`). The doc row is drift and is reported as such rather than tested.

--install-skills installs the Claude Code skills without prompting — unrealizable through the reference recipe: the bundled skills tree is copied next to the entrypoint only by the distributable build, while the recipe builds with `pnpm run build` and invokes `tools/cli/dist/index.js`, so there is no skills bundle for the flag to install and the flag is a silent no-op. Realizing it needs a recipe that builds and invokes the published artifact.

add takes --install-skills — unrealizable through the reference recipe: same cause as `cli-ref-analyze-install-skills-installs-without-prompting` — the entrypoint the recipe builds carries no bundled skills tree, so the flag installs nothing and a scenario would assert against an artifact of the build shape rather than against the product.

TRUECOURSE_HOME relocates the per-user directory — unrealizable under the runner's isolation rule: proving the relocation means asserting on the relocated directory, and the only tree a scenario may assert files in is its working tree — which is exactly where a tool home must never point. The runner already relocates the home for every scenario, so the behavior is exercised everywhere and observed nowhere.
TRUECOURSE_LLM_TRANSPORT overrides the saved transport for one run — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency: the override is only observable on a run that really reaches the model.
TRUECOURSE_MODEL overrides the model globally — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency, and unobservable on the CLI surface: no command prints which model a stage resolved to.
TRUECOURSE_MODEL_<STAGE> overrides the model for one stage — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency, and unobservable on the CLI surface: no command prints a per-stage model resolution.
TRUECOURSE_FALLBACK_MODEL is used when the primary is overloaded — unrealizable: the trigger is the provider returning "overloaded", which the corpus cannot cause without faulting a live provider.
TRUECOURSE_MAX_CONCURRENCY caps concurrent LLM calls across stages — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency, and unobservable on the CLI surface: in-flight call counts are never printed.

the concurrency cap defaults to min(cpus, 4) — unobservable on the CLI surface, and machine-dependent: the default is a function of the host's CPU count, so any assertion would encode the machine that ran it.
TRUECOURSE_MAX_CONCURRENCY also caps the guard runner's parallel sandboxes — blocked-on layer 2 (no `cli/guard` interface) and unobservable: the sandbox count is never printed.
TRUECOURSE_MAX_API_CONCURRENCY caps resident api-driver servers — blocked-on layer 2 (no `cli/guard` interface) and unobservable: the resident-server count is never printed.
the api-driver server cap defaults to min(TRUECOURSE_MAX_CONCURRENCY, 3) — blocked-on layer 2 (no `cli/guard` interface) and unobservable: the derived default is never printed.

TRUECOURSE_LLM_TIMEOUT_SCALE multiplies every per-call timeout on every transport — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency, and unobservable: per-call timeouts are never printed, so proving the multiplication means provoking a timeout at a known duration.
TRUECOURSE_LLM_LOG and TRUECOURSE_LLM_DUMP enable per-call LLM logging — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency: with no LLM call there is no per-call log to write.

TRUECOURSE_DET_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS sets the deterministic scan's per-file budget — already realized as an observation by the flow `survive-a-file-that-exceeds-the-per-file-budget`, authored from analyze/overview.mdx. The cli.mdx restatement is kept as its own claim (the cross-doc rule) but is recorded uncovered rather than re-executed: a second scenario would pay for the same pathological-file run to observe the same thing under a different anchor.

the deterministic per-file budget defaults to 30000 ms — already realized as an observation by the flow `survive-a-file-that-exceeds-the-per-file-budget`, authored from analyze/overview.mdx; recorded uncovered here rather than re-executed, for the same reason as `cli-ref-env-det-file-timeout-sets-the-per-file-budget`.

TRUECOURSE_ROSLYN_HOST points at a prebuilt C# Roslyn host binary — blocked-on the supplied `dotnet-sdk` dependency and on a prebuilt host binary the corpus does not build; the C# host claims are realized once, from analyze/overview.mdx.

TRUECOURSE_NO_PRICE_FETCH skips the model-price fetch — unobservable on the CLI surface: skipping the price fetch changes no printed output and no file in the working tree — the evidence is a network request that did not happen.

TRUECOURSE_TELEMETRY=0 opts out of telemetry — unobservable on the CLI surface: the evidence is a network request that did not happen. Every scenario in this corpus sets the variable, so the behavior is relied on everywhere and observed nowhere.
the CLAUDE_CODE_* variables tune Claude Code mode — blocked-on the supplied `claude-code-binary` dependency, and unobservable: none of the five settings is echoed by any command.
